 OPM's 2027 schedule lists 11 federal holidays. See each date, which ones create a three-day weekend, and which observed days shift.
 1 / 13 List slides 11 federal holidays in 2027, and 9 of them give a three-day weekend List slides Previous Start over By Cris Tolomia · Updated November 16, 2026 Add QZ to Google Illustration: Quartz
 A federal holiday becomes a three-day weekend only when it sits beside a Saturday or a Sunday, and the law settles that in two very different ways. The National Park Service reports that a rule tied to a day of the week sets Martin Luther King Jr. Day, which means the holiday lands on a different date every year. FSIS reports that federal law fixes New Year's Day to a calendar date. That holiday's weekday, and with it the day off, shifts from one year to the next. Holidays tied to a weekday can promise a long weekend years in advance. For holidays tied to a date, the long weekend depends on which weekday the date falls on, and 2027 is an unusually good year for them. Every holiday except Veterans Day and Thanksgiving, which both fall on Thursdays, ends up as a Friday or a Monday off.
 A holiday that falls on a weekend is not lost, because for most federal workers the day off moves into the workweek, right beside the weekend. FSIS reports that when a holiday lands on a Saturday, a worker whose week runs Monday through Friday takes the Friday before it off, while a worker whose week runs Tuesday through Saturday and has a holiday land on Sunday takes the Tuesday after it. The same holiday can produce a different day off for workers on different schedules. Part-time employees are not entitled to a substitute holiday at all, so when a holiday falls on their regular day off, no other day replaces it. A long weekend on the federal calendar is a promise made to the standard full-time schedule, and anyone on a different schedule needs to check how the rules apply to them.
 The U.S. Office of Personnel Management set out to show the official 2027 federal holiday dates for federal employees, from Juneteenth to Columbus Day to Veterans Day. Those dates are the government's own record for its workforce and the baseline for checking any other schedule. The date written into law and the day off are not always the same, and the observed date is the one to plan around. For most employees, a holiday that falls on a Sunday is observed the following Monday. Each holiday raises the same two questions: whether it brings a three-day weekend, and what else the day carries in 2027.
 New Year's Day 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Federal workers start 2027 with a three-day weekend that no weekend-shift rule had to create. New Year's Day is tied by federal law to January 1, according to FSIS , so the holiday keeps its date no matter which weekday that date turns out to be. The U.S. Office of Personnel Management lists the 2027 holiday on Friday, January 1, with no shifted observance attached. Employees on a standard Monday-to-Friday schedule therefore get Friday through Sunday off. For them, the date in the law and the day off are the same day this time, and there is no substitute day to look up. That match does not hold every year, and the two separate again before 2027 is over.
 Anyone planning the end of 2027 should count a second New Year's day off, one that belongs to 2028 but is taken in December. New Year's Day 2028 is a Saturday, so federal employees observe it on Friday, December 31, 2027. Calendar year 2027 therefore holds two New Year's holidays, both on Fridays. A standard federal worker gets two three-day weekends out of them, one in the first days of the year and one in its last. Travel, family visits or a quiet stretch at home can be planned around either, as long as the second one goes on the right day of the calendar.
 For the turn of 2028, put the day off on December 31, not on January 1.
 Birthday of Martin Luther King, Jr. 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Federal workers can count on a three-day weekend for the Birthday of Martin Luther King, Jr. every year, because the holiday is always on a Monday. In 2027 it falls on Monday, January 18, according to the U.S. Office of Personnel Management . That is the holiday's own date and not a substitute day moved from a weekend, and federal staff have Saturday, January 16, through Monday off. The weekday stays fixed while the date moves. The holiday was on Monday, January 19, in 2026 and will be on Monday, January 17, in 2028. Anyone who plans a trip around the 2026 date will book the wrong weekend, so the date has to come from the 2027 calendar.
 King's family meant the holiday as a day of service to others, not a day of rest. "The greatest birthday gift my husband could receive is if people of all racial and ethnic backgrounds celebrated the holiday by performing individual acts of kindness through service to others," Coretta Scott King, Dr. King's wife, said, as reported by the National Park Service. By her measure, the Monday is a day to help someone, and a free day is only part of what it offers. Because the time off is settled in advance, the question for federal workers is what the extra day is for.
 Three days off give people enough time to visit the places where King's work happened. Those places include the Martin Luther King, Jr. National Historical Park in Georgia, the Birmingham Civil Rights National Monument in Alabama, and the Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial in Washington, according to the National Park Service . A visit to any of them ties the long weekend to the person the holiday honors.
 Federal workers never need a lucky calendar for this long weekend, and the only choice they have to make is how to spend it.
 Washington's Birthday 
 Illustration: Quartz
 The law places Washington's Birthday on a Monday, so federal workers get a February long weekend without having to check which weekday the holiday falls on. The holiday's official designation is the third Monday of February, the National Weather Service reports , and in 2027 that day is Monday, February 15, according to the U.S. Office of Personnel Management . The three-day weekend comes from the rule itself rather than from a lucky year on the calendar. Readers need to look up only the date each year, never the weekday.
 With the weekday fixed, the holiday's date changes each year and never matches Washington's actual birthday. In 2028 the holiday falls on Monday, February 21, which is the latest date the holiday can fall on, according to the National Weather Service . Washington was born on February 22, one day after that latest date, so the observed Monday cannot fall on his real birthday in any year. Anyone planning around the holiday should mark the Monday on the calendar, not February 22.
 The holiday most people call Presidents Day appears on the federal schedule under its legal name, Washington's Birthday. That name is set out in Title 5 of the U.S. Code, Section 6103(a), according to the National Weather Service . The Office of Personnel Management and the weather service both make it a rule to use the name in the law, even where a state, a city or a company prefers another name for the day. The different name on the federal calendar is a deliberate choice, not a missing holiday.
 A store sign may say Presidents Day and the federal calendar may say Washington's Birthday, but federal workers get the same Monday off.
 Memorial Day 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Memorial Day gives federal workers a three-day weekend every year, because the law ties the holiday to a Monday rather than to a date. The days off are certain, but the date moves within the last week of May, and in 2027 the holiday comes as late in the month as it can. It falls on the last day of May, Monday, May 31, according to the U.S. Office of Personnel Management . The Federal Reserve Board lists the 2026 holiday on May 25, almost a week earlier, so anyone who reuses the 2026 date in a 2027 plan will book a trip or a rental for the wrong week. In 2027 the break runs from Saturday, May 29, through the holiday Monday. Planners also have no substitute day to find this year. The Monday shown on the federal schedule is the day off, and no weekend shift applies to the holiday on the Federal Reserve's own schedule either.
 The guaranteed Monday had a cost, because the holiday gave up a date of its own to become one. Before the change, Memorial Day was fixed on May 30, according to the National Weather Service . In 2027 May 30 is the Sunday just before the Monday holiday, so the traditional date falls inside the three-day weekend. People who mark the day on May 30 itself don't have to choose this year between the original date and a long weekend away. A standard Monday-to-Friday federal worker gets both.
 In 2027, the original Memorial Day and the federal day off fall on the same weekend.
 Juneteenth National Independence Day 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Federal workers get a long weekend for Juneteenth in 2027 only because the holiday's legal date falls on a Saturday. Federal employees observe the holiday on Friday, June 18, because June 19 is a Saturday in 2027, according to the U.S. Office of Personnel Management . The Friday off sits next to the weekend and gives them a Friday-to-Sunday break. If June 19 fell in the middle of the week, the same holiday would bring no long weekend at all.
 Juneteenth will not move to a dependable Monday, because its date marks a specific day in history. The U.S. Census Bureau reports that General Order No. 3 was issued in Galveston, Texas, on June 19, 1865. "The people of Texas are informed that in accordance with a Proclamation from the Executive of the United States, all slaves are free," Major General Gordon Granger's order said. The holiday keeps the day of that announcement, whatever the weekday. That gives Juneteenth more weight than a convenient Monday would. It also means federal workers get a long weekend only in years when June 19 falls on or next to a weekend.
 The 2027 day off falls on the same date as the first Juneteenth federal holiday. The U.S. Census Bureau reports that the Juneteenth federal holiday was signed into law on June 17, 2021. The first observed holiday came a day later, on Friday, June 18, 2021, and federal employees get that same Friday date off in 2027. The tradition goes back to 1865, but the federal day off is only a few years old.
 Outside the federal workforce, a Juneteenth day off is less certain. Juneteenth has official standing in all 50 states and in the District of Columbia, according to the U.S. Census Bureau , but that standing can be an observance rather than a state holiday. An observance recognizes the day without guaranteeing anyone a day off work. Before planning a three-day trip, workers outside the federal government should check whether their state or employer closes on Friday, June 18.
 Independence Day 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Independence Day gives federal workers a three-day weekend in 2027, with the holiday itself in the middle of it. July 4 is a Sunday this year, so people celebrate on a day most of them already have off rather than on a workday. Federal employees still get a day off for the holiday, on Monday, July 5, according to the U.S. Office of Personnel Management . Their break runs from Saturday through Monday, and the Fourth is the second of those three days. Anyone who stays out late for fireworks on Sunday night still has a full free day before going back to work on Tuesday.
 Anyone who repeats last summer's plans will find the extra day on the other side of the holiday. In 2026, federal employees observed Independence Day on Friday, July 3, so their extra day came before the Fourth rather than after it. Workers get the same number of days off in both years, but a trip takes a different shape. A 2026 getaway could start on Friday morning, while a 2027 trip starts on Saturday and leaves Monday for the trip home. Travelers $TRV who book a rental for the same nights as last year would arrive a day before their time off begins and check out before it ends.
 In 2027, the nation's birthday comes with a day off after it.
 Labor Day 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Labor Day gives federal workers a three-day weekend in 2027 without help from the calendar or from any weekend-shift rule. The holiday falls on Monday, Sept. 6, 2027, according to the U.S. Office of Personnel Management . Standard Monday-to-Friday federal employees therefore get Saturday through Monday off, and nothing has to be moved to make that happen. A holiday that is always observed on a Monday can never fall midweek or on a weekend, so its long weekend is certain every year. That makes Labor Day one of the surest long weekends to plan around in 2027.
 The Monday is fixed, but the date is not, and a person who plans from habit can book the wrong weekend. Labor Day in 2026 is Monday, Sept. 7. Anyone who copies that date into a 2027 calendar plans around the day after the holiday, when the long weekend is already over. The date changes again after 2027, when the holiday falls on Monday, Sept. 4, 2028. A date that is right for one year is wrong for the next, so readers will find the long weekend on a different date in the first week of September each year.
 The day off itself is never in doubt; the one thing to check each year is which Monday it is.
 Columbus Day 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Columbus Day gives federal workers an autumn long weekend that never depends on luck. Under federal law, the holiday falls on the second Monday of October, according to the National Weather Service . The U.S. Office of Personnel Management lists Monday, Oct. 11, as the 2027 holiday, with no shifted observance attached. The date on the schedule is the day off itself, and no weekend rule has to move it. Federal workers can treat the Saturday-to-Monday break as settled and plan a trip around it now.
 Fixing Columbus Day to a Monday cost the holiday its anniversary. Before the change, the holiday was observed on Oct. 12 every year, according to the National Weather Service . Federal workers now get that anniversary off only in years when Oct. 12 is the second Monday, as it is in 2026, and in 2028 the holiday is Monday, Oct. 9. The 2027 date is good for 2027 only, so anyone booking travel for this weekend in a later year needs to look up that year's second Monday instead of reusing this one.
 People argue about what Columbus Day honors, but the dispute has never been about whether federal workers get the day off. In a 2025 Truth Social post, President Donald Trump promised to restore the holiday, and his pledge described the rule that was already in force. "I am hereby reinstating Columbus Day under the same rules, dates, and locations, as it has had for all of the many decades before!" Trump said, as reported by TIME. Congress has not removed Columbus Day from the federal holidays, so the pledge brought back nothing that had been taken away. Congress has also never given Indigenous Peoples Day federal holiday status, even though former President Joe Biden recognized it on the same Monday as Columbus Day. The name a president favors is a political choice, while the law keeps the Monday off in place.
 Whatever people call it, the 2027 day off is Monday, Oct. 11, and nothing in the naming fight has changed that.
 Veterans Day 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Veterans Day gives federal workers a single midweek day off in 2027, not a three-day weekend. The holiday is tied to the date of Nov. 11 rather than to a weekday, and in 2027 that date is a Thursday, according to the U.S. Office of Personnel Management . The weekend-shift rules apply only to holidays on a Saturday or Sunday, so a Thursday holiday stays where it is. A federal worker gets the day free and then goes back to work on Friday before the weekend begins.
 Federal workers get a long weekend for the holiday again a year later. In 2028, Nov. 11 is a Saturday, and federal employees take Friday, Nov. 10, as the observed holiday, with three days off in a row. Veterans Day's weekday changes from one year to the next, so a midweek holiday in one year can turn into a long weekend in the next. Anyone hoping for a long November weekend around Veterans Day should look to 2028.
 Veterans Day began as Armistice Day, the Census Bureau reports , and the veterans it honors today come from two very different generations. Post-9/11 veterans were the largest group in 2025, at 31.4% of all veterans. Those who had reached age 75 or older made up nearly as big a share that year, at 30.5%. The day is about recent wars as much as old ones, and Americans who mark it honor an elderly generation alongside a much younger one.
 A midweek Thursday is a fitting date for a day with that weight. It is a day to mark, not a break to plan around.
 Thanksgiving Day 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Thanksgiving always falls on a Thursday, so it gives federal workers a holiday but never a long weekend on its own. In 2027 the day off is Thursday, November 25, according to the U.S. Office of Personnel Management . That leaves one ordinary weekday, Friday, between the holiday and the weekend. A Thursday holiday can never land on a Saturday or a Sunday, so the rules that move a weekend holiday into the workweek never apply to it. The date on the schedule is the day off, and nothing about it moves closer to the weekend. On the federal calendar, Thanksgiving stands alone as a Thursday holiday.
 The weekday stays the same every year, while the date changes. Thanksgiving falls on Thursday, November 26, in 2026 and on Thursday, November 23, in 2028. A family can plan the shape of the break years ahead, even though it has to look up the date each time. Every Thanksgiving trip or gathering starts from a Thursday holiday, never from a Friday or a Monday, and the federal government gives one day off for it. The Friday after Thanksgiving is not a federal holiday. Anyone who wants four days in a row has to arrange that Friday separately, with annual leave or with an employer's own schedule.
 For Thanksgiving, readers have to build the long weekend themselves.
 Christmas Day 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Federal workers get a three-day weekend for Christmas in 2027, but their paid day off is Christmas Eve, not Christmas Day. Christmas is on a Saturday this year, so the U.S. Office of Personnel Management lists Friday, Dec. 24, as the observed holiday for federal employees. The year's last federal holiday therefore comes with a break that runs from Christmas Eve through Sunday, and Christmas itself falls in the middle of it rather than at its start. Federal workers who usually spend Dec. 24 at their desks and wrap up last errands after work can treat that Friday as a full free day this year. Anyone who plans around a federal schedule in 2027 should mark Dec. 24 as the day off, not Dec. 25.
 A long Christmas weekend is common in the years around 2027, and what changes from year to year is which day federal workers actually get off. In 2026, Christmas is on Friday, Dec. 25, so the long weekend begins on the holiday itself and no day needs to move. In 2028, Christmas is on Monday, Dec. 25, so the holiday ends a long weekend rather than starting one, and the day off and the holiday are again the same day. Of those three years, 2027 is the only one in which the paid day off and Christmas are different days. In 2027, someone who keeps the habit from those other years and marks Dec. 25 as the day off will put it on a Saturday, when federal offices are already closed.
 Even the most familiar date on the federal calendar is worth checking for its observed day before anyone books travel or sets a family gathering.
